_metadata.name: Named Stars Catalog — for heliacal rising and stellar-event tracking
source_notes: Star positions (RA/Dec) at J2000.0 from the Hipparcos catalog via standard reference.
Heliacal rising significance follows the named cultural attestation.
Stars chosen for cultural and ritual significance across multiple traditions.
_metadata.epistemic_tag: [SOURCE: Hipparcos / classical astronomy for positions; multi-tradition for cultural attestations]

stars.name: Sirius
stars.significance: The brightest star in the night sky. Its heliacal rising marked the start of the Egyptian New Year and predicted the annual Nile flood (~mid-July at Egyptian latitudes). The Sothic cycle of 1,460 years aligned the civil and Sothic Egyptian calendars. Sacred to Isis in Egyptian tradition.
stars.heliacal_significance: Egyptian agricultural year start; Sothic cycle anchor

stars.name: Pleiades (Alcyone)
stars.significance: The most famous open star cluster. Heliacal rising marked the start of the agricultural / sailing season across many premodern cultures (Hesiod's Works and Days advises sowing at their setting). In the Chinese 28-mansion system, the Pleiades are mansion 17 (Mǎo 昴, the Hairy Head).
stars.heliacal_significance: Agricultural new year across Mediterranean and Andean cultures; Beltane fires in Celtic tradition

stars.name: Spica
stars.significance: The reference star of Chinese mansion 0 (Jiǎo 角, the Horn of the Azure Dragon). In Vedic tradition, the principal star of the Citrā nakshatra. Used by ancient navigators as a reference; its position helped establish the precession by Hipparchus.
stars.heliacal_significance: Marks the spring planting season in temperate latitudes

stars.name: Antares
alt_names: Xīn 心 (Chinese — Heart of the Azure Dragon)
stars.significance: The 'Rival of Mars' — red supergiant whose color competes with Mars. Reference star of Chinese mansion 4 (Xīn 心, the Heart of the Azure Dragon). One of the four 'Royal Stars' of ancient Persia (with Aldebaran, Regulus, and Fomalhaut).
stars.heliacal_significance: Mid-summer marker in northern temperate latitudes

stars.name: Aldebaran
stars.significance: The Bull's Eye in Taurus. Reference star of Chinese mansion 18 (Bì 畢, the Net). One of the four Royal Stars of ancient Persia (the Eastern Watcher).
stars.heliacal_significance: Late-spring marker in northern temperate latitudes

stars.name: Regulus
stars.significance: The 'Little King' — α Leonis. One of the four Royal Stars of ancient Persia (the Northern Watcher / Heart of the Lion).
stars.heliacal_significance: Late-summer marker

stars.name: Fomalhaut
stars.significance: One of the four Royal Stars of ancient Persia (the Southern Watcher). Brightest star in the southern celestial vicinity in autumn northern-hemisphere skies.
stars.heliacal_significance: Autumn marker

stars.name: Vega
stars.significance: The fifth-brightest star. Will become the pole star around 14,000 CE due to precession (it last was the pole star around 12,000 BCE). In the Chinese Qixi myth, Vega is the Weaver Girl separated by the Milky Way from Altair the Cowherd, meeting only on the 7th night of the 7th lunar month.
stars.heliacal_significance: Summer marker; will be future pole star

stars.name: Altair
stars.significance: The Eagle's brightest star. The Cowherd in the Qixi myth — meets the Weaver Girl (Vega) once a year across the Milky Way (Magpie Bridge).
stars.heliacal_significance: Late-summer marker (Qixi festival)

stars.name: Betelgeuse
alt_names: Shēn 參 (Chinese, the Three Stars / Orion)
stars.significance: Red supergiant in Orion's shoulder. Visually striking; expected to supernova within the next 100,000 years. In the Chinese 28-mansion system, Orion's belt is mansion 20 (Shēn 參).
stars.heliacal_significance: Winter marker; signal of Orion's seasonal visibility

stars.name: Rigel
stars.significance: Blue supergiant in Orion's foot. Brightest star in Orion (despite Bayer's β designation).
stars.heliacal_significance: Winter marker

stars.name: Capella
stars.significance: The 'She-Goat' in Auriga the Charioteer. Sixth-brightest star in the night sky; brightest star within 30° of the north celestial pole.
stars.heliacal_significance: Marker of late autumn in temperate northern latitudes

stars.name: Procyon
stars.significance: Eighth-brightest star. 'Procyon' = 'before the dog' — rises before Sirius (the Dog Star).
stars.heliacal_significance: Pre-Sirius rising as Egyptian agricultural precursor

stars.name: Polaris
stars.significance: The current pole star (closest approach c. 2100 CE). Used as the canonical northern reference for navigation in the modern era.
stars.heliacal_significance: N/A — circumpolar at most northern latitudes; never rises or sets

stars.name: Thuban
alt_names: Pole Star of the Bronze Age
stars.significance: The pole star around 2787 BCE — aligned with the descending passage of the Great Pyramid of Giza. A dim star but historically critical.
stars.heliacal_significance: Egyptian Old Kingdom pole-star reference

stars.name: Canopus
stars.significance: Second-brightest star in the night sky after Sirius. Not visible from most of Europe; primary southern-sky beacon. Used by Polynesian and Arab navigators.
stars.heliacal_significance: Southern navigation reference

stars.name: Achernar
stars.significance: Brightest star in the river Eridanus. Far southern declination; not visible from most of Europe.
stars.heliacal_significance: Southern hemisphere marker

stars.name: Arcturus
stars.significance: Fourth-brightest star in the night sky. 'Bear-Guardian' — Greek myth links it to keeping watch over the Great Bear (Ursa Major).
stars.heliacal_significance: Spring marker in northern temperate latitudes

stars.name: Deneb
stars.significance: The 'tail' of Cygnus the Swan. One of the three stars of the Summer Triangle (with Vega and Altair). Will be a near-pole star around 10000 CE.
stars.heliacal_significance: Summer Triangle marker

stars.name: Alphecca
stars.significance: Brightest star of the Northern Crown — Ariadne's crown in Greek mythology.
stars.heliacal_significance: Late-spring marker

stars.name: Rigil Kentaurus (α Centauri)
alt_names: Nán Mén 南門 (Chinese — Southern Gate)
stars.significance: Third-brightest star in the night sky. Closest star system to the Sun (4.37 ly). Visible only from southern latitudes.
stars.heliacal_significance: Southern hemisphere navigation marker

stars.name: Alkaid
alt_names: Yáoguāng 摇光 (Chinese — Last of the Seven)
stars.significance: Last star in the handle of the Big Dipper. One of the seven canonical stars of the Northern Dipper (北斗) in Chinese astronomy.
stars.heliacal_significance: Circumpolar in northern latitudes — always visible
